benchmark.origin: Existing phase6 chronological synthetic generator; no amount modifications
benchmark.selected_explanation: Amount is 3.33x the prior reference median (8.230 currency units; category and direction, 56 training examples). Robust log amount deviation: 4.90. No supported recurring due date matched. Decision threshold: 3.5000, strict greater-than; calibrated on 245 prior reference rows through 2025-04-30. Calibration rank is not a probability. Unusual activity is not confirmed fraud.

scenes.caption: A freelancer can have income on paper and still run short before the next payment. CashGuard explores that gap locally.
Fictional demo data. Opening cash is an explicit assumption; reconstructed balances are estimates, not bank balances.
The existing engine projects recurring events and residual cash flow over 30 days. These are conditional estimates, not guarantees.
This separate labeled synthetic benchmark contains deliberate amount changes. The default engine genuinely flags this example; unusual does not mean fraud.
Back to the standard demo. A hypothetical emergency expense changes the same event ledger; it does not change recorded history.
Gemma 3 runs through local Ollama on computed evidence. It explains the analytics; Python still calculates every financial amount.
Calibration is separate from the synthetic final holdout. Benchmarks support reproducibility, not claims of real-world accuracy. Hosted CI is not yet verified.
A local early-warning workspace for cash-flow questions. No bank connection, financial-advice service, fraud confirmation, customers or revenue are claimed.
